what: whether token_aug's run-to-run variation looks like a selection flip or accumulation order, by counting distinct outputs over identical repeated calls

plain_token_aug_0.reading: no element moved over any run

token_aug_64.reading: the largest delta is 16.2x the mean output magnitude on 0.648% of rows. Reordering a sum cannot do that; a different set of contributions can. This does NOT identify what changed -- the admitted set is not observable from here -- it rules out the benign explanation

control_other_block.reading: a block stage 2 found bitwise reproducible. If this is not deterministic here, the harness is measuring something other than what stage 2 measured.

cannot_settle: proof of a selection flip. Clustering is consistent with a small candidate space and also with a kernel that varies accumulation across a few fixed schedules; reading a cluster count as a set count is the error to avoid.
which set is correct. This asks only whether the answer is stable.

hypotheses_tested_and_refuted.why_recorded: both are the obvious first guesses, both are wrong, and each cost minutes to eliminate against hours to rediscover.

centroid_fidelity.hypothesis: token_aug selects by the query block's CENTROID, and the 2026-08-15 morton work measured that a fragmented block's centroid represents its members worse than a compact one's. Blocks are raster-ordered here (morton off), so poor centroids could put the selection near a tie.
centroid_fidelity.refuted_by: our own numbers. Per-block centroid fidelity was measured at blocks 24 and 49 (workflows/h3_config.py, the morton_curve note): 0.7915/0.9434 under 3d and 0.7665/0.8804 under 2d_frame. Block 49 has the BETTER centroids of the two depths sampled, under both curves, and it is the unstable one. The hypothesis needs the opposite.
centroid_fidelity.not_concluded: that centroid quality is irrelevant. Two depths were sampled and fidelity may simply not predict tie-proximity, which is a different property of the same distribution.

high_norm_rows.hypothesis: docs/evidence.md records that what survived the withdrawal of the 'block 49 carries 4x the error' claim was a large exact-stage hotspot 'in a few high-norm rows'. The unstable rows are also few, so they might be those rows.
high_norm_rows.refuted_by: measured 2026-09-08 on this cell. Of 455 rows that move, ZERO are in the top-455 by per-row v L2 norm, against a chance level of 0.44%. Their median norm is 0.93x the rest and their median norm-rank percentile is 74.9%, so they sit in the lower three quarters rather than the top.
high_norm_rows.not_concluded: that the hotspot is not real. It was measured under a different metric on a different question; this says only that the unstable rows are not it.

still_open.what_varies: the admitted token SET is not observable from outside the kernel, so nothing here says what changes between launches, only that a reordered sum cannot account for it.
still_open.why_this_block: two explanations eliminated, none established. Block 49 is the last DiT block, which nothing here has tested as relevant.
still_open.does_it_reach_a_render: cannot, today: token_aug ships off in every graph.
